newsitem.title: UK: LVMH buys Grand Met shares, bid ruled out.
newsitem.headline: LVMH buys Grand Met shares, bid ruled out.

text.p: French luxury goods company LVMH said Tuesday it had bought shares in Grand Metropolitan Plc but has no intention of making an offer for the British beverage company.

In a surprise move, LVMH, which is trying to block a planned merger between Grand Met and Guinness Plc, said it now owned 0.23 percent of Grand Met after buying 4.75 million Grand Met shares at an average price of 577 British pence ($9.43) per share.
Grand Met, whose holdings include the Burger King fast-food chain, and LVMH were not immediately available for comment.
The move comes hard on the heels of LVMH's request last week for an arbitration proceeding to settle the dispute with Guinness, in which LVMH holds a 14.2 percent stake.

LVMH contends it has the right to buy Guinness's stake in their joint distribution ventures and in champagne and spirits group Moet Hennessy if Guinness goes ahead with the Grand Met merger which, if approved, would be the biggest in British corporate history.
The complex merger is also being closely watched by the European Commission, which is still considering whether to start a full probe into the proposed merger.
LVMH's main argument against the merger is that, under the terms of agreements signed with Guinness, a change in control would enable LVMH to operate its joint ventures with Guinness independently.
Guinness has said that LVMH's claims lack any legal basis and is confident the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), which will oversee arbitration, would agree.
